feature: Text typed on a screen is drawn clean
summary: Words typed onto a screen you are designing no longer get the soft white glow that keeps a caption readable over a photo. Captions on the open canvas, and on a boundary drawn around a screenshot, still get it.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to turn on. The difference only shows on a screen whose surface is not white, so paint one first.

try.do: Press T, click on a dark part of the picture, and type Gap 16. Look at the soft light edge around the words.
Press F and drag out a screen beside it.
With the screen picked, set Background in the Frame section to a strong colour.
Press T, click on the screen, and type Gap 16 again.
Compare the two: same words, same colour behind them, only the one on the picture is haloed. Before this change both were.
Double click the heading on the screen and look at Enable Shadow in the dock: it reads off, because off is what is drawn.
Drag the heading off the screen onto the canvas. The halo comes back. Drag it back on and it goes again.

evaluate: Does the heading on the screen look like type on a screen now, rather than type on a photo?
Is keeping the halo on a caption over a screenshot still the right default?
A screen only counts once it paints a background, so a boundary drawn with Frame Selection around a capture leaves captions alone. Is that the line you would draw?
The Shadow switch reads off for text on a screen, and turning it on gives real shadow. Is off the honest reading, or would you rather see the halo listed and switchable?
If you put a screenshot inside a screen and caption it, the caption comes out clean. Is that wrong enough to fix?
rough: On a white screen, which is what the frame tool makes by default, this change is invisible: a white halo behind dark text cannot be seen against white. The complaint only bites once a screen has a colour, so the pictures here paint one.

The rule reads the container, not what is under each word. A caption laid over a screenshot that sits inside a painted screen loses its halo. Turning the Shadow switch on gives it a real shadow, but nothing tells you that is the way back.

The two pictures are crops of real window captures from Scripts/playtest/screen-text-halo-walk.json, the before taken with the rule switched off in a scratch build. Full window shot: 2026-09-03-screen-halo-window-sc.png.
